name: Protection visa (subclass 866, onshore) / Refugee and Humanitarian Program (offshore)

application_window.note: The offshore Humanitarian Program operates under an annual planning level (places), distinct from the uncapped onshore protection visa process

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being physically in Australia at the time of application.
This requires meeting the refugee definition (Geneva Convention grounds) or complementary protection criteria (real risk of significant harm if returned).
This requires a UNHCR referral (Refugee visa) or an eligible proposer in Australia (Community Support Program / Woman at Risk / other humanitarian streams).

evidence_required.document: Evidence supporting the persecution or serious-harm claim

sources.title: Protection visa (subclass 866) - Department of Home Affairs

notes: Consistent with the same permanent-on-grant pattern seen throughout Australia's skilled visa system in this dataset (189, 190, 186, 858) — both onshore Protection visas and most offshore Humanitarian Program visas grant PERMANENT residence directly, unlike the temporary-then-permanent staged approach used by most European asylum routes in this dataset (Germany's 3/5-year staged permits, Netherlands' 5-year permit, Portugal's 3-year permit). This is a genuinely favourable structural feature worth surfacing prominently: a successful humanitarian applicant in Australia reaches the same permanent status as a successful skilled migrant, immediately, rather than facing a multi-year renewal/reassessment cycle first. No application fee for onshore Protection visa applications, consistent with the no-fee pattern seen on every other country's asylum route in this dataset.
